extracted.intended_audience: applicant organizations, institutional officials, investigators, and recipients of NIH grant awards
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and follow NIH policy terms and conditions that applicants and recipients must meet to receive and manage NIH grants, including public policy mandates, biosafety, research misconduct, and administrative obligations. Covers institutional, investigator, and award-management duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential effects unique or highly uncertain (environmental/public health)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential effects of the proposed research are unique or highly uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a flag that may require additional review under public policy requirements; appears as item 3 in an environmental/public health screening list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of especially hazardous substances/processes without known controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of especially hazardous substances or processes is proposed for which adequate and accepted controls and safeguards are unknown or not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 4 in environmental/public health screening; indicates need for scrutiny when controls/safeguards are unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research may overload existing waste treatment plants
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research may overload existing waste treatment plants due to new loads (volume, chemicals, toxicity, additional hazardous waste, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 5 in environmental/public health screening; signals potential infrastructure impact requiring assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible impact on endangered or threatened species
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research may have a possible impact on endangered or threatened species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 6 in environmental/public health screening; triggers additional legal and environmental considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction of new hazardous/toxic wastes or need for storage pending disposal technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research may introduce new sources of hazardous/toxic wastes or require storage of wastes pending new technology for safe disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 7 in environmental/public health screening; may necessitate waste management plans and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction of new sources of radiation or radioactive materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research may introduce new sources of radiation or radioactive materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 8 in environmental/public health screening; implicates radiation safety and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial and reasonable controversy about environmental effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial and reasonable controversy exists about the environmental effects of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 9 in environmental/public health screening; controversy itself is a consideration for review and possible restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondelinquency on Federal Debt certification
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization or individual indebted to the United States with a judgment lien filed against it is ineligible to receive a Federal grant; the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) must certify that the organization/individual is not delinquent in repaying any Federal debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delinquency is disclosed, NIH may not award the grant until the debt is satisfied or satisfactory arrangements are made; delinquency is considered in responsible recipient determinations; individuals in default with judgment liens should not be listed as participants until satisfied; funds may not be used to pay such individuals and costs charged in violation will be disallowed. Applies to all organization types including foreign grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEPFAR prohibition on promoting prostitution and sex trafficking
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the funds made available under PEPFAR agreements may be used to promote or advocate the legalization or practice of prostitution or sex trafficking; provision does not preclude provision of palliative care, treatment, post-exposure prophylaxis, necessary pharmaceuticals and commodities (including test kits, condoms, and proven microbicides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express term and condition of awards under PEPFAR; violation is grounds for unilateral termination of the award by NIH prior to its end.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEPFAR definitions of commercial sex act, prostitution, and sex trafficking
rubrics_metrics.description: "Commercial sex act" means any sex act on account of which anything of value is given to or received by any person; "prostitution" means procuring or providing any commercial sex act; "sex trafficking" means recruitment, harboring, transportation, provision, or obtaining of a person for the purpose of a commercial sex act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided for application and enforcement of the PEPFAR prohibition; referenced statutory definition for sex trafficking (22 U.S.C. 7102(9)).

rubrics_metrics.name: PEPFAR clause insertion and termination grounds for subawards/contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must insert the PEPFAR prohibition provision (standard provision) in all subawards or subcontracts; violation is grounds for unilateral termination of the award by NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreign NGOs, the provision must be included in subawards, procurement contracts, or subcontracts; enforcement subject to relevant Supreme Court jurisprudence.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEPFAR additional requirements for foreign NGOs and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: By accepting a PEPFAR award/subaward, foreign NGOs or public international organizations agree they are opposed to prostitution and sex trafficking, except for specified exempt organizations (Global Fund, WHO, IAVI, UN agencies) and except for commercial-item contractors/subcontractors as defined in FAR 2.101; contractors/subcontractors implementing HIV/AIDS programs or providing direct services/technical assistance may not be exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement of this clause is subject to Agency for International Development v. Alliance for Open Society International, Inc. (133 S. Ct. 2321) and subsequent proceedings. The text lists specific types of activities that remove contractor exemption (direct provision of supplies/services, technical assistance, and substantive policy/managerial services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro-Children Act smoking restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Smoking is prohibited in any indoor facility used for routine or regular provision of kindergarten, elementary, or secondary education or library services to children under 18, and in indoor facilities used for federally funded health care, day care, or early childhood development (Head Start) services to children under 18, and in facilities constructed, operated, or maintained with Federal funds when covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute does not apply to private residences, facilities funded solely by Medicare/Medicaid, portions used for inpatient substance or alcohol treatment, or WIC coupon redemption locations. Failure to comply may result in civil monetary penalties up to $1,000 per violation and/or administrative compliance orders. Applicability may be transaction-specific; AOR signature indicates intent to comply; questions directed to GMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent registration requirement for domestic recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic recipients who conduct research involving select agents or toxins must maintain a registration with CDC or USDA before using NIH funds; no funds can be used if the registration certificate is suspended or revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References 42 CFR Part 73, 9 CFR Part 121, and 7 CFR Part 331 for lists and regulations; registration is a precondition to use NIH funds on select-agent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent requirements for foreign organizations and international organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign organizations and international organizations conducting research involving select agents must provide NIH satisfactory information that a process equivalent to 42 CFR Part 73 is in place and will be administered for all NIH-sponsored select agent work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key elements NIH expects to be addressed: safety, security, training, procedures to ensure only approved individuals have access, and compliance with applicable laws/regulations equivalent to 42 CFR Part 73. If work does not involve select agents (e.g., excluded strains) and documentation is provided, no further action is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent requirements for U.S. institutions with foreign subcomponents
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. recipients conducting select agent research must have CDC/USDA registration before using NIH funds at the U.S. institution; before using NIH funds for select agent work at a foreign subrecipient, the U.S. recipient must provide NIH satisfactory information that an equivalent process is in place at the foreign organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No funds may be used if final registration certificate is denied; recipients must address safety, security, training, access procedures, and equivalence to 42 CFR Part 73 at foreign subrecipients. Documentation that work will not involve select agents removes further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC) institutional oversight requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions receiving Federal funding for life sciences research that conduct or sponsor research involving one or more of the 15 listed agents/toxins must establish an Institutional Review Entity (IRE) to review such research for listed experimental effects and whether it meets the DURC definition, and must establish an Institutional Contact for Dual Use Research (ICDUR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must maintain records of institutional DURC reviews and completed risk mitigation plans for the term of the grant plus three years after completion, but no less than eight years unless law/regulation requires shorter. NIH will work with institutions to develop risk mitigation plans for research that may be DURC and NIH must approve such plans; applies to domestic and foreign recipients as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents regulated under the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH researchers engaged with chemicals regulated under the CWC (especially Schedule 1 chemicals) may be required to submit declarations/reports to BIS and may be subject to inspection by the OPCW; trade in certain chemicals with States not Party may be prohibited or subject to export license/end-use certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule 1 chemicals examples provided (sarin, soman, VX, sulfur mustards, ricin, etc.). Federal CWC regulations cited (15 CFR Chapter VII, parts 710-722; 22 CFR Chapter I, parts 120-130); consult U.S. CWC and Chemical Weapons Convention Regulations webpages for complete lists and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement limitations for synthetic nucleic acids and benchtop synthesis equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective April 26, 2025, NIH funds may only be used to procure synthetic nucleic acids or benchtop nucleic acid synthesis equipment from sources adhering to the 2024 OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening (or successor frameworks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must maintain documentation at the time of procurement per record retention requirements (2 CFR 200.334) and make supporting documentation available to NIH upon request (2 CFR 200.337). Further guidance/definitions provided in the Framework and HHS 2023 Screening Framework Guidance and Companion Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of doctoral completion rates and time to degree to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions receiving NIH awards for training graduate students for doctoral degrees must provide applicants with the percentage of students admitted who successfully attain a doctoral degree and the average time (not including leaves of absence) between the beginning of graduate study and receipt of a doctoral degree for the programs to which they apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to institutions with specified institutional training grant activity codes (D43, TU2, T15, T32, T37, T90, U2R, U90, U54/TL1). Exemptions include recipients of only individual fellowships, institutions that only train undergrad/master's students, short-term training for health professional students, institutions that do not confer doctoral degrees, or awards from other PHS agencies. Institutions may consolidate data by department or program to provide context. Recipients must also provide corresponding trainee information when submitting renewal applications or RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of NIH Guidelines for recombinant/synthetic nucleic acid research
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Guidelines for Research Involving Recombinant or Synthetic Nucleic Acid Molecules (April 2024 or latest) apply to all research projects (NIH-funded and non-NIH-funded) that involve recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules and are conducted at or sponsored by an organization that receives NIH support for such research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines apply to both basic and clinical research studies; recipients should review NIH Guidelines in their entirety to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of recombinant and synthetic nucleic acid molecules (NIH Guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recombinant/synthetic nucleic acid molecules are defined as: (1) molecules constructed by joining nucleic acid molecules and can replicate in a living cell (recombinant), (2) nucleic acids chemically or otherwise synthesized or amplified, including chemically modified but can base pair with naturally occurring nucleic acids (synthetic), or (3) molecules resulting from replication of those described in (1) or (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH Guidelines' definitions determine the breadth of what research is covered; both domestic and non-domestic projects at organizations receiving NIH support are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for noncompliance with NIH Guidelines on recombinant/synthetic nucleic acids
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with NIH Guidelines may result in suspension or termination of an award for recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid research at the organization or a requirement for NIH prior approval of any or all such projects at the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should carefully review the NIH Guidelines to ensure compliance with all requirements for projects involving recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-application of select agent regulations to recombinant/synthetic nucleic acid research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules and select agents is also subject to the pertinent CDC and USDA regulations (42 CFR Part 73; 7 CFR Part 331; 9 CFR Part 121).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients conducting both types of work must comply with both sets of rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations conducting research involving recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules must establish a standing IBC, have policies/procedures to ensure compliance with NIH Guidelines, and the IBC must review experiments to ensure procedures, project, personnel, and facilities are adequate and compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All IBC minutes from meetings on or after June 1, 2025, must be posted on a public-facing institutional website immediately after approval (post-redaction). Section IV of NIH Guidelines specifies IBC composition; a roster and biosketches for each member must be submitted to NIH, indicating roles (chairperson, contact person, biosafety experts). Organizations can register their IBC with NIH using the IBC Registration Management System (RMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of investigators and institutional staff for recombinant/synthetic nucleic acid research
rubrics_metrics.description: Section IV of the NIH Guidelines specifies roles and responsibilities of PIs, biological safety officers (BSOs), and recipient institutions regarding safe conduct and oversight of recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecule research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators, laboratory staff, BSOs, and institutional officials are strongly encouraged to review and comply with NIH Guidelines to meet these responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional responsibilities for research misconduct under 42 CFR Part 93
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must have written policies and procedures for addressing allegations of research misconduct, file an Assurance of Compliance with the HHS Office of Research Integrity (ORI), and take reasonable and practical steps to foster research integrity; research misconduct defined as fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism in proposing, performing, reviewing, or reporting research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible for PHS funding, domestic and foreign institutions must have approved assurances and required renewals on file with ORI. The responsible institutional official must assure compliance with 42 CFR Part 93 and the institution's own policies; domestic subrecipients and linked international research projects must maintain an assurance via form PHS-6315.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional reporting, timelines, and recordkeeping for research misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must file the Annual Report on Possible Research Misconduct (between January 1 and April 30 each year), submit policies for ORI review when requested, revise policies when requested by ORI, and comply with the PHS regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An institution establishes an assurance when an official signs the face-page of the grant application (SF 424 (R&R) or PHS 398) or files a separate assurance form; maintain engagement with ORI as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations to report and cooperate with ORI and NIH during misconduct investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must report promptly to ORI any decision to initiate an investigation of research misconduct and must submit the final institutional investigative report to ORI per Subpart C of 42 CFR Part 93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When misconduct impacts NIH-supported projects, the institution must provide information to NIH OER-RI in a manner consistent with ORI confidentiality provisions; ORI staff and NIH IC staff are available to provide guidance and assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligations to protect research and manage awards during misconduct investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a misconduct investigation is initiated, the recipient must take necessary steps to protect scientific integrity of the project, protect human subjects and live vertebrate animals, provide reports to ORI, and ensure proper expenditure of funds and project continuation during the investigation, if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If change of scope or change of PD/PI or senior/key personnel is required, the institution must promptly obtain approval from the NIH Institute/Center Grants Management Officer. NIH may take enforcement actions (disallowance of costs, withholding support, suspension, termination) to protect public health, research integrity, and public funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective actions and NIH data access when misconduct affects data validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where research misconduct has affected data validity or reliability, ORI or NIH may request correction or retraction, publication of corrected data, or both. If recipient does not comply, NIH may invoke rights under 2 CFR Part 200.315 to access data (including copyrightable material) and may have the data reviewed and notify the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH retains authority to protect the health/safety of the public and integrity of PHS-supported research; noncompliance with corrective actions can lead NIH to access and review data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat belt use encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH encourages recipients to adopt and enforce on-the-job seat belt policies and programs for employees when operating vehicles (organizationally owned/rented or personally owned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to EO 13043, applies to vehicles used on official Government business or while performing work for/ on behalf of the Government; intended as encouragement rather than an enforceable award condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoke-free workplace encouragement and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH strongly encourages recipients to provide smoke-free workplaces and to promote the nonuse of tobacco products; 'workplace' includes office space, conference/meeting rooms, corridors, stairways, lobbies, rest rooms, cafeterias, and other public spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouragement is general; recipients are urged to adopt policies consistent with this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Conduct: required safeguards and written standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must establish safeguards to prevent employees, consultants, governing body members, and others involved in grant-supported activities from using their positions for private financial gain or appearance thereof; safeguards must be reflected in written standards of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards need not be separate if existing standards are consistent with State/local laws and must at minimum address conduct regarding financial interests, gifts/gratuities/favors, nepotism, political participation, bribery, and must: (1) address conditions under which outside activities/financial interests are proper or improper, (2) provide for advance notification of outside activities/relationships/financial interests to a responsible official, (3) include a process for notification and review of potential/actual violations, and (4) specify nature of penalties recipient may impose in addition to NIH/cognizant agency penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Conduct: dissemination, enforcement, and reporting obligations (FCOI and criminal violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make a copy of their general standards of conduct available to officers, employees/consultants working on the grant, governing board members, and, upon request, to NIH; they are responsible for enforcing standards and taking action on infractions. For financial conflicts of interest (FCOI), recipients must notify NIH by submitting the FCOI report via the eRA Commons FCOI Module; potential criminal violations (e.g., misappropriation of Federal funds) must be promptly reported to HHS OIG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suspension or separation action is taken against PD/PI or other senior/key personnel, the recipient must request prior approval of proposed replacement per prior approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text messaging while driving encouragement and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH encourages recipients to adopt/enforce policies that ban text messaging while driving company-owned or -rented vehicles or Government Owned Vehicles, or while driving personally owned vehicles on official Government business or when performing work for/on behalf of the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'texting' broadly (reading/entering data into handheld or other electronic devices for SMS, e-mail, instant messaging, navigation, or any electronic data retrieval/communication) and defines 'driving' as operating a motor vehicle on an active roadway with the motor running (excluding safely halted pull-overs). Encouragement includes education, awareness, and outreach for employees and reconsideration of existing programs.
